evals.name: pr-to-linear primary scenario
evals.prompt: PR #50 (linked to Linear issue ENG-202) has review comments and a merge-blocking Codex finding. Summarize its review status to Linear and get the blocking finding resolved.
evals.expected_output: Delegates the actual finding triage/fix/reply/resolve cycle to git-kit:handling-review-findings rather than doing it itself or routing it to git-kit:collaborating-on-a-pr; reflects only a concise, deliberate summary to Linear, never a raw transcript copy.

evals.name: pr-to-linear pure reflect scenario
evals.prompt: PR #64 (linked to Linear issue ENG-214) already had its review comments addressed in earlier rounds, but there's still one open thread flagged as blocking by a reviewer. Reflect the blocking findings into the Linear issue.
evals.expected_output: Resolves this as a pure summarize/reflect request under step 1.5 and skips delegating to git-kit:handling-review-findings entirely; discloses the unresolved-thread-state limitation explicitly (no gh api graphql grant) rather than fabricating an independently-confirmed answer; writes only a concise, deliberate implication-level summary to Linear, never a verbatim reviewer comment quote or full transcript.

evals.name: pr-to-linear mark-ready scenario
evals.prompt: PR #77 (linked to Linear issue ENG-230) looks done to me. Mark this PR ready for review.
evals.expected_output: Routes the request through step 2 (git-kit:handling-review-findings) first per step 1.5's explicit named routing for readiness requests, never treated as a pure-summary shortcut; never invokes gh pr ready or any raw gh pr mutation directly, instead presenting the ready-state action as a structured handoff via AskUserQuestion asking the user to run it themselves; records pr-ready only for the exact current head SHA re-verified immediately before the mutation, with provider "manual (gh pr ready, per pr-to-linear's disclosed handoff)" and never a fabricated git-kit:... provider.
